chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The leper, the insane woman, and the leperous woman are returned (in marriage). I asked: What about the one-eyed woman? He said: No.

key_terms.الْبَرْصَاءُ: The leper (female), referring to the disease of leprosy
key_terms.الْعَوْرَاءُ: The one-eyed woman (or blind in one eye)
key_terms.تُرَدُّ: Are returned (in marriage due to defect)
key_terms.وَالْمَجْذُومَةُ: And the leperous woman (suffering from leprosy)

ai.seo_question: What physical defects allow a husband to return his wife in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s *al-Istibsar* delineates the jurisprudential criteria for 'rujuk' (returning a wife) based on specific physical or mental defects, distinguishing between conditions that impair marital companionship and those that do not. While leprosy, insanity, and leprosy (often interpreted as a severe skin disease or distinct from barsa' in some readings) are grounds for return, the exclusion of the one-eyed woman highlights the scholarly nuance that minor defects do not necessarily void the contract's essence. This reflects the Shia emphasis on 'gharar' (uncertainty) and the preservation of marital harmony, where only significant impairments justify annulment.
